rv.q: It's bigger, better and more brilliantly bungling than ever.
It is impossible not to be swept along by the giddily escalating mirth of Matt DiCarlo's amiable production.
Mischief is a creative, comedic powerhouse, and the clever storyline and talented cast make About Spies not only a spectacular spy spoof but also an outstanding show altogether.
If you like Mischief's previous work, you will love this. If you are new to their style, it's a fabulous introduction.
Ultimately, it's escapism of the highest order, and in the end, hugely enjoyable.
Their latest show, an espionage spoof, improvised and scripted, strong on wordplay, is as silly and as funny and as absurd as their past productions.

From the creative team that brought you The Play That Goes Wrong in 2012 (and assorted sequels) comes this spy caper. As ever with Mischief productions, their latest work is a lot of fun and pays its dues to the great age of British farce (and pantomime too) with clever wordplay and physical comedy as things go increasingly awry.
The brilliant minds of Mischief have done it again, delivering another incredibly clever slapstick comedy that will have you laughing until you can’t breathe.
It's wonderful. Mischief at their best, as finely worked as clockwork and exuberant as toddlers.
The show's worth seeing for this 'pre-credits' sequence alone, but do stick around for the rest of it.
